finding2_sidecars.harmful_or_untidy: untidy, not harmful: the -wal was 0 bytes (no unflushed data), PRAGMA integrity_check was 'ok' and the copy read correctly without them; but while a connection is open the companions are REQUIRED, so deleting them under a live connection would be unsafe.
finding2_sidecars.root_cause: SQLite's backup API copies the database header, which records the WAL write-version; store.init_db sets the source to WAL, so the run-scoped copy was itself WAL and materialised -wal/-shm on any read/write. A stage connection left open (materialize/review call store.connect(ctx.db_path)) kept them after ctx.con.close().
finding2_sidecars.copy_rows_match_source_note: Proven by guard (d) on a fresh run whose stages do not write: all 12 table counts equal the source. The stale pre-fix copy differs on dockets (7 vs 2) because U8.3's run legitimately wrote dockets into its working copy; its own row counts were preserved exactly through the conversion.
